title: Biweekly team update — November 3, 2026
jerry: Matmul main includes contiguous host address remapping, a tiled output canvas and software tiling tests. Next: record tiled board pass logs and resolve full-canvas DMA reachability.
stephanie: Selected attention MatMul runs through MNN and Jerry’s 16×16 FPGA array in 320 PIO jobs. The integrated image runs at 80 MHz after timing issues at 90 MHz. Single-run results were 5.74% faster for zeros and 2.71% slower for nonuniform input; repeated measurements and real-image accuracy checks remain pending.
tiffany:
Baseline and Profiling on full Tiny-Vit 21M model inference, measured a latency of 7.64s for 1 thread FP32, and 5.07s for 1 thread INT8, and 3.19s for 2 thread INT8 configuration.
 Profiled FP32 and INT8 operator runtimes. GELU and Gemm were the largest groups in the INT8 model, accounting for approximately 30.7% and 27.0% of logged layer time, helping identify priorities for optimization and FPGA acceleration.
  Conducted accuracy comparison of FP32 vs. INT8 over 2000 images from IMAGENET. INT8 has a Top1 accuracy drop by 1.3% compared to using FP32.
  Next: repeat matched CPU/FPGA benchmarks, measure transfer and control overhead, and compare integrated inference accuracy and latency against the CPU baseline.

Peripheral Setup 
 Set up and connected the USB camera to the DE1-SoC board.
 Confirmed that the board can receive live image input from the camera.
 Next: connect camera capture and image preprocessing to our FPGA-accelerated model pipeline for end-to-end live image classification, then verify predictions and measure camera-to-classification latency.
winnie:
- SIMD: On the Cortex-A9, 32×32 int8 matmul took 94.67 µs with NEON versus 202.12 µs in plain C (2.13× faster), with matching results. Used GCC -O3, 1,000 warmups and 10,000 timed runs.
- Softmax: Implemented 16-bit fixed-point softmax for up to 196 values using 33-cycle unsigned restoring division. All 147 rows / 8,666 outputs matched Python exactly; standalone timing passed 90 MHz using 222 ALMs and 10 M10Ks. Next: matmul integration and full-system testing.
- GELU: Bias + GELU is connected to accel_top’s CPU output-read path, processing 16 int8 lanes with a 256-byte bias buffer. Standalone timing passes 90 MHz; logic usage fell from 1,707 to 957 ALMs.
notes: Coordinate matmul, nonlinear-unit and MNN interfaces. Keep standalone 90 MHz timing separate from the integrated 80 MHz image. Collect matched benchmark and verification evidence for the next professor meeting.
